Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings • 2-day history of constant suprapubic burning pain, ↑ urinary frequency, pink urine, mild nausea, subjective fever; no dysuria or flank pain. • No prior similar episodes; healthy baseline. • Possible pregnancy though low likelihood with Implanon.

Working diagnosis • Uncomplicated acute cystitis — supported by suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, hematuria, systemic symptoms. Empiric trimethoprim commenced.

Differential considerations (consistent with transcript & DDx) • Early appendicitis – monitor for migration of pain, worsening nausea/vomiting, RLQ tenderness. • Ectopic pregnancy – low but must be excluded; advised home pregnancy test. • Pelvic inflammatory disease – less likely given lack of discharge or dyspareunia, but consider if symptoms evolve.

Management • Trimethoprim 300 mg* PO BID × 3 days (*dose per doctor’s verbal instruction; strength not documented). • Paracetamol for analgesia. • Encourage oral hydration; cranberry juice optional. • Pregnancy test to be performed. • Safety-net advice: return or call if worsening pain, fever, vomiting, or no improvement in 48–72 h. • Doctor to arrange further investigations (urinalysis, culture, bloods, imaging) if no improvement.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute cystitis – High likelihood. Matches suprapubic pain, urinary frequency, hematuria, mild systemic features.  
2. Acute appendicitis – Medium likelihood. Gradual peri-umbilical pain, nausea, subjective fever; monitor for progression.  
3. Ectopic pregnancy – Low–medium likelihood. Reproductive-age female with abdominal pain; Implanon lowers but does not eliminate risk.
